pr_title: EVP_DecodeUpdate() should not produce padding zeros to the decoded output (Fixes #26677)
pr_body:
EVP_DecodeUpdate() should not produce zeros for input padding `=` signs to avoid writing to non-allocated memory regions.

To achieve this:
- Add `eof` parameter to `evp_decodeblock_int` function in `openssl/crypto/evp`. The parameter should either contain the number of the input padding characters to ignore or `-1` if the function has to count them.
- Use precalculated `eof` in `EVP_DecodeUpdate` to fix its behaviour.
- Use `eof = -1` in `EVP_DecodeFinal` to count it in `evp_decodeblock_int`.
- Do not ignore padding in `EVP_DecodeBlock` (`eof = 0`) because it should write padding zeros according to the documentation.

pr_comments: If this PR is accepted, should I create similar PRs for older minor versions (3.4, 3.3, 3.2, 3.1, and 3.0) and for 1.1.1 and older, if applicable?
How does the new code behave with input like `AAAA====` (3 or 4 trailing `=` padding chars)?

> @vdukhovni
> How does the new code behave with input like `AAAA====` (3 or 4 trailing `=` padding chars)?

I enumerate the parts of my answer for easier discussion of them:
1. I checked: `EVP_DecodeUpdate()` returns `-1` (decoding error) as expected on `AAAA====`.
2. `EVP_DecodeFinal()` should fail if the number of the input base64 characters is not a multiple of four. However, if the number of symbols in the buffer is a multiple of four by this moment, this signifies serious trouble or misuse I believe
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/53cef57c0804cf512e833d05b6972e7cca98e068/crypto/evp/encode.c#L442-L443
3. The behaviour of `EVP_DecodeBlock` should not have changed because `eof=0` means the old behaviour (converting trailing `=` to zeros), but I did not check it and did not find any separate tests for it. I can write a few test applications if needed, though.
4. A negative test covering the case of redundant padding characters already exists and passes
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/c152a943957933e8aa621441a36e9951f7eff050/test/recipes/30-test_evp_data/evpencod.txt#L48-L51
5. The higher-level call to `EVP_DecodeUpdate` creates a counter called `eof` and increments it on every `=`, which allows the program to monitor the number of padding characters
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/53cef57c0804cf512e833d05b6972e7cca98e068/crypto/evp/encode.c#L338-L339
6. If this counter is greater than `2` or if there are any base64 symbols after `=`, the function returns `-1`
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/53cef57c0804cf512e833d05b6972e7cca98e068/crypto/evp/encode.c#L340-L349
7. The latter case (symbols after padding) was also covered by tests
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/c152a943957933e8aa621441a36e9951f7eff050/test/recipes/30-test_evp_data/evpencod.txt#L56-L58

We DO NOT do merge commits, the history of each OpenSSL branch is linear.  Your changes need to be relative to master and not contain any merges.

You need to fetch a fresh master branch from the openssl/openssl repo. Then do `rebase -i master` and drop all the merge commits from the rebase. It should produce clean commits on top of the current master branch.
Please also note that there is no need to synchronize the branch unless there are conflicts reported in the Github PR UI.
